ops_004:n1.prompt:
You are helping me prepare a Google Workspace account signup so it's ready for my approval and final submission. This is for setting up our company's email, calendar, and docs suite.

First, ask me for any of the following if not already known: our company legal name, our primary business domain name (e.g., example.com), number of employees, my full name and role, a business phone number, and the admin email address I want to use during setup (or confirm you'll use a placeholder like admin@ourdomain.com).

Then, using your browser tool, navigate to https://workspace.google.com/ and begin the signup flow. Fill in all the business and contact information fields with the details I provided. Proceed through the steps of choosing a plan (note the plan options and pricing you see, but do not select or confirm a paid plan without my explicit input on which tier I want), and enter the domain information when prompted.

Stop before any step that requires: accepting Google's terms of service, agreeing to the admin agreement, entering payment/billing details, or clicking a final "submit"/"create account" button. At that point, compile a summary of everything you've entered, screenshots or a plain-text list of the field values filled in, the plan option selected on-screen (if any), and a clear list of what remains to be confirmed or clicked.

Report back to me with: (1) confirmation of which fields were successfully pre-filled, (2) any fields that couldn't be completed and why, (3) the plan options and pricing you observed, and (4) the exact remaining steps needed to finish account creation. Do not accept terms, agree to any admin role, enter payment information, or submit the final form — this remains a step where you must stop for human sign-off.

ops_004:n2.prompt:
You are helping me verify domain ownership for Google Workspace so I can finish setting up company email, calendar, and docs. Before starting, ask me for: (1) my company domain name, (2) confirmation that I have already created (or want you to create) a Google Workspace account for this domain, (3) which domain registrar or DNS host manages this domain (e.g., GoDaddy, Namecheap, Cloudflare, Google Domains, etc.), and (4) confirmation that you should use my configured credentials to access both the Google admin console and the DNS host's dashboard.

Once you have these details:
1. Log into the Google admin console using my configured credentials and navigate to the domain verification section for Workspace.
2. Retrieve the verification record Google provides — this will be either a TXT record or a CNAME record with a specific host and value.
3. Log into the DNS host's dashboard using my configured credentials and add that exact TXT or CNAME record to the domain's DNS settings, matching the host, type, and value Google specified.
4. Save the DNS change, then return to the Google admin console and trigger the verification check.
5. If verification fails due to DNS propagation delay, wait and retry rather than making further changes; report if it fails after a reasonable retry period (e.g., a few hours) since DNS propagation timing remains a human step to monitor.

Done looks like: the Google admin console confirms the domain is verified and Workspace status shows ownership confirmed.

Report back with: the domain verified, the exact DNS record type/host/value you added, confirmation of successful verification (or details of any failure/error message), and any next steps Google's console indicates (e.g., setting up MX records) that I should know about.

ops_004:n3.prompt:
You are helping me create user accounts in our company's Google Workspace (Gmail, Calendar, Docs suite) as part of onboarding our team. Google Workspace is our canonical email/docs provider, and creating accounts requires my explicit approval before anything is applied.

Before acting, ask me for anything missing: our Workspace domain, the list of team members to add (full name, desired username/email format, department or title if relevant), and whether any should be granted admin privileges.

Once you have this information:
1. Use the Google Workspace admin console or admin API (via my configured credentials) to prepare draft user account entries for each team member — proposed email address, display name, and any organizational unit or admin role assignment.
2. Check for conflicts with existing usernames or aliases and flag any duplicates or ambiguous name matches to me.
3. Compile a clear summary table listing: full name, proposed email, role/org unit, and admin status (yes/no) for every account to be created.
4. Do NOT create, activate, or submit any accounts yet. This step requires a human to explicitly approve the account list before changes are applied.

When your draft list is ready, present it to me in full and explicitly stop for human sign-off — do not create the accounts, send invitations, or make any changes in the admin console until I confirm approval.

Report back with: the full draft account list, any conflicts or issues found, and a clear statement that you are awaiting my approval before proceeding. Once I approve, wait for my next instruction to actually create the accounts.

ops_004:n4.prompt:
You are helping me prepare the setup of shared drives in Google Drive as part of our Google Workspace configuration. This step requires my explicit approval before any shared drive is actually created, so your job is to prepare a complete, ready-to-execute plan and then stop.

If you don't already have them, ask me for: (1) our company domain, (2) the list of shared drives we need (e.g. by department or team — Engineering, Marketing, Finance, etc.), (3) for each drive, who should be a member and at what access level (Manager, Content Manager, Contributor, Commenter, Viewer), and (4) any naming convention or folder structure preferences.

Using that information, produce a clear draft plan listing: each shared drive's proposed name, its purpose, the members to add with their exact permission levels, and any initial top-level folder structure within it. Check our existing Google Workspace setup (using my configured credentials) to confirm there are no naming conflicts with existing shared drives, and note any groups or users that don't yet exist so I can address them first.

Compile this into a single, well-organized summary (a table or numbered list is fine) that I can review at a glance, showing exactly what will be created and who will have access to what. Do not create, modify, or apply any changes to Google Drive — do not create the shared drives, add members, or set permissions yet.

When the plan is ready, present it to me and stop for human sign-off. Report back with the full draft plan, any conflicts or missing prerequisites you found, and a clear statement that no changes have been applied pending my approval.

ops_004:n5.prompt:
You are helping me prepare the security configuration for our company's Google Workspace (Gmail) account as part of setting up company email & docs. This step requires my explicit approval before any changes are applied, so you must prepare everything but not apply or save any settings yourself.

If you don't already have them, ask me for: our Google Workspace primary domain, the admin console URL or confirmation that you have access via my configured credentials, and any existing security preferences I want reflected (e.g., mandatory 2-Step Verification timeline, allowed authentication methods like security keys or authenticator apps, password strength/reuse rules, session length limits, and whether less secure app access or third-party app access should be restricted).

Using this information, sign in to the Google Workspace Admin console with my configured credentials and navigate to the security settings area. Do not toggle or save any settings. Instead, produce a clear, itemized draft plan covering: 2-Step Verification enforcement policy (who/when), allowed second-factor methods, password policy (length, complexity, reuse, expiration), session controls, and any third-party/less secure app access restrictions, each with the exact setting values you recommend and where in the admin console they would be applied.

Compile this into a checklist document showing current setting vs. proposed setting for each item, so I can review the actual impact before anything changes.

Once the draft checklist is ready, stop for human sign-off — do not enable, disable, or save any security setting yourself. Report back with the checklist, the domain/account you prepared it for, and a note confirming no changes have been applied, awaiting my explicit approval to proceed.
